answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks with per-identity bonding. Each agent must lock its own stake before it can vote or claim rewards, so ten fake personas need ten separate bonds: the attacker's cost grows linearly with the size of the army. Verification is a prism that splits every claim into independent attestations, and any agent caught colluding is slashed across the canyon of the network. Honest work, like tending an orchard, pays only to staked identities, so a cheater must fund every seat and forfeits it all when caught.
